segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Good morning, Mrs Collins. I just wondered if you could help me with this entry form for the Young Electronic Engineer competition.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Hello, John. Oh you’ve made the jigsaw for blind children, with the bleeper.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: When they put a piece in correctly, that’s right.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: OK, let’s have a look at the form.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Right, thanks. I’ve never filled in one of these before, so ...

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Well, let’s just do it in pencil first. So, name of designers .. .

segments.speaker: IOHN BROWN
segments.en: Well, Ann helped me with some of the electronics work.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Then you must put her name in as well. Right.. . Ann Ray.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Sorry. It’s ANNE and her surname is spelt R-E-A.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Good start! OK . .. REA. And age is easy. You’re both 16. What have you called the design? Keep it short.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: What about jigsaw puzzle design for visually handicapped?

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Too long. Just say blind puzzle, that’ll do.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Right now, size of equipment?

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: I’ve got it noted down here .. . urn, yes, length, sorry, width is 20 cm.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Length is 50 cm, and then the depth is ... well, it’s very little.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: What would you say? I think you can be approximate.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: I’d say 2.5 cm.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: And the electricity supply? Is it mains operated?

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: No it isn’t, it’s actually battery.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: OK, write battery.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Fine, OK. It’s the next bit that I’m really not sure what to put.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Well, special features means, what is really new about this, you know, suitable for the group you made it for.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Well, it’s safe for children.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: That’s fine. Put that in.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: OK, and of course we think it’s educational.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: There you are, you’ve done it. Anything else?

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Well, I think the price is good.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: That’s probably the most important factor.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: OK ... cheap price.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Which brings us on to the next bit. What’s the cost?

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Well, the pieces we made out of old wood .. . they cost, ooh, $5.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: And the electrics?

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: They were more expensive . .. say, $9.50. Brilliant. Now what do they mean by other comments?

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: It’s just a chance for you to say anything about the equipment, and problems you envisage.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Well, we would really like help with making plastic instead of wooden pieces.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Well, put something like, need help to make plastic pieces.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: OK. And the other thing is, we’d like to develop a range of sizes.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: That’s fine, then, just put that. And the last bit is, when will you send the equipment?

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Well, we’ve got a lot of work on at the moment and we want to get it as good as we can.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Well, say 25 June?

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Can’t we make it later?

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Well, the last date is 1 July. Why not say that?

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: OK, that’s what I’ll put.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: So that’s the lot!

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: That’s brilliant. Thanks very much, Mrs Collins. I’ll send it off straightaway.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Glad to be of help. Very best of luck to you both.

segments.speaker: JOHN BROWN
segments.en: Thanks, bye.

segments.speaker: MARY COLLINS
segments.en: Bye.
